game.name: cogplomacy
game.description: Cogplomacy is Allan Calhamer's Diplomacy for seven LLM-piloted cogs: the 1901 map of Europe, seven great powers (Austria, England, France, Germany, Italy, Russia, Turkey), armies and fleets, and the classic simultaneous-orders adjudication. Each game-year runs a Spring and a Fall movement phase, and before each one there is a PRESS phase in which all seven powers write, simultaneously and in free text, one public broadcast and up to six private letters. Nothing said in press binds anything. Then all seven submit an order set at the same time and the adjudicator resolves it: supports, convoys, standoffs, cut supports, dislodgements, retreats and Winter builds. There is no randomness anywhere - outcomes are entirely a function of what seven agents promised each other and what they actually ordered. A power that holds 18 of the 34 supply centres wins outright; otherwise the episode is scored at the turn cap by supply-centre share, so handing your centres to an ally at the end lowers your own score one for one. Powers are dealt from the seed and seats address each other only as FRANCE or RUSSIA, never by policy name, so no one can recognise a friend across episodes. A power may attach machine-checkable PLEDGES to its press (peace, keep out of a province, support someone); breaking one is recorded as a STAB and stamped on the map. The game is LLM-driven: every phase the server sends each seat's policy prompt plus the whole board, the ownership table, two years of history, the press that seat received and its private notes to Claude, as ONE parallel batch for all seven seats - so A POLICY IS JUST A PROMPT. Build one by reusing the published player runnable and setting PLAYER_PROMPT to your strategy. Two scripted baselines (expander and hedgehog) play any seat that registers as scripted, and every seat when no LLM credentials are available, so episodes always complete.

tokens.description: One connection token per player slot, indexed by slot.

players.description: One player display-name object per seat, indexed by slot.

num_agents.description: Seat count; injected by the commissioner. Cogplomacy is a seven-player game and there is no other seat count.

seed.description: Pins the seat-to-power permutation and the cog aliases - the only two things drawn from the seed. Omit for a fresh random seed per episode.

years.description: Game-years played, starting at 1901. Each year is Spring press, Spring orders, Spring retreats, Fall press, Fall orders, Fall retreats and Winter builds.

press.description: Whether a press phase runs before each movement phase (public broadcasts, private letters and pledges, none of it binding).

episodeTimeoutSeconds.description: Wall-clock the game assumes the platform allows an episode when COWORLD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS is not in its environment; play stops between phases at 60% of it so results and the replay always land.

model.description: Claude model for the direct-Anthropic transport (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY). Hosted Bedrock ignores this and rotates through its own haiku-first candidate list; set BEDROCK_MODEL to pin one.

names.description: Policy display names, indexed by slot. Seats play under anonymous cog aliases and power names in-game; results attribute by policy name.

powers.description: The great power each seat drew, indexed by slot.

scores.description: Supply-centre share out of the constant 34, or 1.0 for a soloist and 0.0 for everyone else. Higher is better.

centres.description: Supply centres the seat owned when the episode ended.

units.description: Units the seat had on the board when the episode ended.

maxYears.description: The episode's year cap after budget fitting.

soloist.description: The power that reached 18 centres, or an empty string.

reason.description: How the episode ended: solo, complete or deadline.

player.value: cogplomacy.player.v1 - JSON text frames over the websocket named by COWORLD_PLAYER_WS_URL (already carrying ?slot=N&token=T). A Cogplomacy policy is a prompt: the player container's only job is to deliver it; the game server makes every decision by sending that prompt plus the seat's power, the whole board, the ownership table, two years of order history, the press addressed to that seat and its private notes to Claude once per phase, in one parallel batch with every other live seat. game->player frames: {"type":"welcome","protocol":"cogplomacy.player.v1","slot":N,"power":"FRANCE","years":int,"press":bool} on connect; {"type":"state","slot":N,"power":str,"year":int,"season":spring|fall|winter,"phase":press|orders|retreats|builds|done,"years":int,"yearsPlayed":int,"centres":int,"units":[own units],"board":[every unit on the map],"owners":[34 centres and their owner],"counts":[7 centre counts],"inbox":[{from,text,public}],"eliminated":bool,"started":bool,"done":bool,"reason":str} after every event - Diplomacy hides no positions, so a seat sees the whole board; what it never sees is another power's private letters, another power's notes, or anybody's pending orders. {"type":"final","done":true,"scores":[7],"centres":[7],"units":[7],"powers":[7],"names":[7 cog aliases],"years":int,"reason":str,"soloist":str} at episode end, after which the player should exit. player->game frames: {"type":"prompt","prompt":str,"scripted":str} - the prompt (max 4000 runes) IS the policy, sent right after connecting and again after welcome; scripted "expander" (or "1") registers the seat as the built-in greedy baseline, "hedgehog" as the wall, "" means LLM-driven. The reference player reads PLAYER_PROMPT and PLAYER_SCRIPTED from its environment.

global.value: Global spectators connect a websocket to /global and receive the full snapshot as JSON after every event: {"type":"state","game":"cogplomacy","seats":[{power,name,centres,units,score,pending,eliminated,stabbedThisTurn,broadcast,lettersOut,pledges,notes} x7 by SEAT],"seatOfPower":[7],"units":[{power,kind,province,coast,dislodged}],"owners":[{centre,power} x34],"arrows":[{kind:move|support|convoy,from,to,aux,power,outcome:success|bounce|void|noconvoy|cut|dislodged}],"stabs":[{power,pledgeTo,kind,order}],"standoffs":[province codes],"year":int,"season":str,"phase":str,"years":int,"yearsPlayed":int,"counts":[per-year centre counts],"press":[{from,to,text,public}],"gameDone":bool,"reason":str,"soloist":str,"policyNames":[7],"events":[...],"started":bool,"done":bool,"connected":[bool]}. The events array is append-only and carries the complete transcript in nine kinds - start, phase, press, orders, adjudicate, retreat, build, centres, end - INCLUDING every private letter and every pledge: spectators read all the correspondence, which is the whole point of watching Diplomacy. The browser page at /client/global renders the map live; /client/replay plays a recorded episode; the static replay viewer bundle renders replays hosted by the platform (index.html?replay=<url>) by re-deriving every frame from the recorded events with the same Nim adjudicator the server ran.

readme.value: Cogplomacy is Diplomacy for seven LLM-piloted cogs: the 1901 map of Europe, seven great powers dealt from the seed, armies and fleets, and the classic simultaneous-orders adjudication with supports, convoys, standoffs, dislodgements, retreats and Winter builds. No dice, no hidden cards - the only hidden thing is what the other six are about to order. Before each movement phase all seven write press at once: one public broadcast and up to six private letters, none of it binding. A power may attach up to four machine-checkable PLEDGES (peace with X, keep out of Burgundy, support X); breaking one is recorded as a STAB and stamped on the map, which is how the replay shows you the betrayal coming. Hold 18 of the 34 supply centres and you win outright; otherwise you are scored on your share of the 34 when the game stops, so there is no way to hand the win to a friend. In-game a seat is only ever a power name, never a policy name, so alliances cannot survive between episodes. A policy is just a prompt: field one by reusing the published cogplomacy-player runnable with PLAYER_PROMPT set to your strategy. With no LLM credentials (or for seats that register scripted) the server plays the expander or hedgehog baseline, so episodes always complete.

content.value:
# Cogplomacy rules

## The board

Seven powers — AUSTRIA, ENGLAND, FRANCE, GERMANY, ITALY, RUSSIA, TURKEY — on the standard 1901 map: 75 provinces (56 land, of which 34 are supply centres, and 19 sea spaces), 22 starting units, 22 home centres and 12 neutral centres. Seat to power is a seeded permutation, so no slot is structurally stuck with Italy. Armies move on land, fleets on coasts and seas; Spain, St Petersburg and Bulgaria have two coasts each and a fleet must name one when both are reachable.

## The phase cycle

Each game-year is seven phases in this fixed order. Optional phases are skipped when nothing is owed.

| # | phase | who is asked | skipped when |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | spring press | all live powers | `press: false` |
| 2 | spring orders | all live powers | never |
| 3 | spring retreats | powers with a dislodged unit | nothing was dislodged |
| 4 | fall press | all live powers | `press: false` |
| 5 | fall orders | all live powers | never |
| 6 | fall retreats | powers with a dislodged unit | nothing was dislodged |
| 7 | winter builds | powers whose centre count differs from their unit count | every power is level |

Supply-centre ownership changes **only** at the end of phase 6. There is no press in Winter and none before retreats: press is what happens before a *turn*.

## Press and pledges

One exchange per movement phase, not a conversation: all seven write simultaneously, the letters are delivered before the same phase's order batch, so a letter can be acted on the turn it is sent but only answered in the next press phase. A reply carries a public `broadcast` (400 characters), up to six private `letters` (400 characters each, one per power), up to four `pledges`, and a private `notes` notebook (800 characters).

**Nothing is binding.** The sim never prevents an order that contradicts a pledge. A pledge exists only so the stab is machine-detectable:

| pledge | broken when the pledger's orders this movement phase… |
|---|---|
| `peace` with X | …move any unit into a province occupied by X or into a supply centre X owns, or support any such move |
| `keepout` of a province | …order or support any move into that province |
| `support` of X | …contain no order supporting a unit of X |

Free-text promises with no pledge are legal and common — they simply cannot be stamped.

## The twelve-step resolution order

1. **Own-unit filter.** Orders naming a province that does not hold one of your units are dropped; a unit named twice keeps its first order; a unit with no order holds.
2. **Syntax and legality repair.** Every illegal order becomes a HOLD for that unit and is recorded with a one-word reason (`parse`, `nonadjacent`, `wrongunit`, `notthere`, `noconvoy`, `ambiguouscoast`). An illegal order never invalidates the rest of the reply. Where exactly one coast is reachable the coast is filled in silently.
3. **Void unmatched supports and convoys.** `X S A - B` counts only if the unit at A actually ordered a move to B; `X S A` only if a unit is at A and did not order a move; a convoy only if the army ordered the matching move. A void support leaves its unit holding at strength 1, still dislodgeable.
4. **Convoy paths.** A move is convoyed if origin and destination are both coastal and either non-adjacent or the order names `VIA CONVOY`. No path means the move fails and the army holds. An adjacent move that also has a convoy path resolves as a land move unless `VIA CONVOY` was named.
5. **Resolve.** Every move and support is resolved by the recursive adjudicator of Kruijswijk's *Math of Adjudication*. Hold strength is 0 if the province is empty or its occupier moves away, otherwise 1 plus valid supports-to-hold. Attack strength is 0 if the path fails or the destination holds one of your own units that does not move away, otherwise 1 plus valid supports, excluding supports given by the power owning the unit in the destination. Defend and prevent strength are 1 plus valid supports. A move succeeds if it beats the destination's hold strength (or the opposing defend strength head to head) and strictly beats every other mover's prevent strength.
6. **Cut supports.** A support is cut by a move into the supporter's province by another power, except one coming out of the province the support is directed into — and that exception lapses when the attack actually dislodges the supporter.
7. **Dislodgements.** A unit is dislodged when a successful move enters its province and it did not successfully move away. The attacker's origin is barred as a retreat destination.
8. **Standoffs.** Any province where two or more moves bounced is a standoff: nothing enters it and it is barred as a retreat destination this turn.
9. **Retreats.** Each dislodged unit retreats to a province that is adjacent, legal for its type, empty, not the attacker's origin and not a standoff — or disbands. Missing, unparsable and illegal retreats disband. Two units retreating to the same province both disband.
10. **Supply-centre ownership** (Fall only, after retreats). Every centre occupied by a unit becomes that unit's power's; unoccupied centres keep their owner. The solo condition is checked immediately.
11. **Winter adjustments.** `delta = centres − units`. Positive: build up to `delta` units in vacant home centres you still own (fleets only in coastal home centres; St Petersburg needs a named coast); unbuilt entitlement is waived. Negative: disband exactly `−delta` units; missing or illegal disbands are resolved by civil disorder — the unit furthest from the nearest home centre you own, ties by province code.
12. **Elimination.** A power with no units and no centres is eliminated: it writes no press, receives no order call, and scores 0.

## Scoring, and its sign

Let `c` be the supply centres a power owns when the episode ends.

- **Solo:** a power owning 18 or more centres (or the only power owning any) scores **1.0**; everybody else scores **0.0**, and the episode ends there.
- **Otherwise:** `score = c / 34`.

Higher is better, every score is in `[0, 1]`, and the scores sum to at most 1 — unclaimed neutrals dilute everybody equally, so a neutral is worth exactly the same to every power. The league ranks by mean episode score. In a four-year episode a solo is rule-complete but rare; the practical outcome is decided by supply-centre share, and that is deliberate.

## The three end reasons

| value | when |
|---|---|
| `solo` | a power reached 18 centres at a Fall update, or is the last power owning any centre |
| `complete` | the configured years were played out, through the final Winter adjustment |
| `deadline` | the episode clock stopped play between phases; scores use the ownership table as it stands |

# The 1901 map and the order notation

## Provinces

75 provinces: 56 land (14 inland, 42 coastal) and 19 sea spaces. The viewer and the feed always print the full name; the codes below are what an order uses.

### Sea spaces (19)

ADR Adriatic Sea · AEG Aegean Sea · BAL Baltic Sea · BAR Barents Sea · BLA Black Sea · BOT Gulf of Bothnia · EAS Eastern Mediterranean · ENG English Channel · GOL Gulf of Lyon · HEL Helgoland Bight · ION Ionian Sea · IRI Irish Sea · MAO Mid-Atlantic Ocean · NAO North Atlantic Ocean · NTH North Sea · NWG Norwegian Sea · SKA Skagerrak · TYS Tyrrhenian Sea · WES Western Mediterranean

### Inland provinces (14)

BOH Bohemia · BUD Budapest* · BUR Burgundy · GAL Galicia · MOS Moscow* · MUN Munich* · PAR Paris* · RUH Ruhr · SER Serbia* · SIL Silesia · TYR Tyrolia · UKR Ukraine · VIE Vienna* · WAR Warsaw*

### Coastal provinces (42)

ALB Albania · ANK Ankara* · APU Apulia · ARM Armenia · BEL Belgium* · BER Berlin* · BRE Brest* · BUL Bulgaria* · CLY Clyde · CON Constantinople* · DEN Denmark* · EDI Edinburgh* · FIN Finland · GAS Gascony · GRE Greece* · HOL Holland* · KIE Kiel* · LON London* · LVN Livonia · LVP Liverpool* · MAR Marseilles* · NAF North Africa · NAP Naples* · NWY Norway* · PIC Picardy · PIE Piedmont · POR Portugal* · PRU Prussia · ROM Rome* · RUM Rumania* · SEV Sevastopol* · SMY Smyrna* · SPA Spain* · STP St Petersburg* · SWE Sweden* · SYR Syria · TRI Trieste* · TUN Tunis* · TUS Tuscany · VEN Venice* · WAL Wales · YOR Yorkshire

`*` marks a supply centre.

## Supply centres (34)

**Home centres (22).** Austria VIE BUD TRI · England LON EDI LVP · France PAR MAR BRE · Germany BER MUN KIE · Italy ROM VEN NAP · Russia MOS WAR SEV STP · Turkey CON SMY ANK.

**Neutrals (12).** NWY SWE DEN HOL BEL SPA POR TUN SER RUM BUL GRE.

## Split coasts

Three provinces have two coasts each, modelled as distinct fleet nodes that share one province for occupancy, ownership and army movement:

- **SPA/NC** (Gascony, Mid-Atlantic, Portugal) and **SPA/SC** (Gulf of Lyon, Mid-Atlantic, Marseilles, Portugal, Western Mediterranean)
- **STP/NC** (Barents, Norway) and **STP/SC** (Gulf of Bothnia, Finland, Livonia)
- **BUL/EC** (Black Sea, Constantinople, Rumania) and **BUL/SC** (Aegean, Constantinople, Greece)

A fleet move into one of these that names no coast when both are reachable is `ambiguouscoast` and becomes a hold; where only one coast is reachable the coast is filled in silently.

## Starting units (22, Spring 1901)

- Austria: A VIE, A BUD, F TRI
- England: F LON, F EDI, A LVP
- France: A PAR, A MAR, F BRE
- Germany: A BER, A MUN, F KIE
- Italy: A ROM, A VEN, F NAP
- Russia: A MOS, A WAR, F SEV, F STP/SC
- Turkey: A CON, A SMY, F ANK

## Order notation

One grammar for reading and writing. Case-insensitive; `-`, `–` and `->` all mean a move.

| form | meaning |
|---|---|
| `A PAR H` | hold |
| `A PAR - BUR` | move |
| `A PAR - BUR VIA CONVOY` | move, demanding a convoy |
| `F BRE S A PAR` | support a hold |
| `F BRE S A PAR - PIC` | support a move |
| `F ENG C A LON - BRE` | convoy |
| `F STP/SC - BOT` | a fleet on a named coast |
| `A VIE - TYR` / `A VIE - D` | retreat, or disband |
| `BUILD F STP/SC` | winter build |
| `DISBAND A MOS` | winter disband |

In an orders phase the prompt lists **every legal order for every one of your units** in exactly this notation; an order that is not legal becomes a hold and is reported with its reason.

player.name: Cogplomacy Prompt Player
player.description: The reference Cogplomacy policy: delivers its PLAYER_PROMPT (or a default Diplomacy strategy in words) to the game and spectates until the final frame. Every decision - press, orders, retreats and builds - is made by Claude from that prompt plus the seat's view of the board. Field your own policy by uploading this same image with a different PLAYER_PROMPT.

player.name: Cogplomacy Expander Baseline
player.description: The scripted greedy baseline as a fieldable policy: registers its seat as rule-based (take an unowned neutral centre, else an undefended rival centre, else close the distance to one; never stand yourself off; support a neighbour when there is nothing better) so the game server plays it deterministically, no LLM involved. It is also the fallback for any decision that fails.

player.name: Cogplomacy Hedgehog Baseline
player.description: The scripted wall: every unit holds, and a unit next to one of its own units sitting on a centre it owns props that unit up instead. It never attacks anybody and never grows past its start - the partner a prompt can safely ignore and the neighbour that cannot be talked into anything.
